change: No changes. Primary Upper Traps + Rhomboids confirmed by EMG research on prone incline shrug. Lower Traps and Posterior Deltoid as secondary confirmed. All buckets and latin terms valid.

No changes. Quads, Glutes (Maximus + Medius), and Adductors as primary confirmed — research shows Gluteus Medius activation is 20-30% higher in lateral lunges vs other lunge variants, supporting its primary status. Hamstrings (secondary on lunge per rules), abs, and obliques (bilateral step but frontal-plane anti-lateral trunk tilt) as secondary confirmed.

No changes. Biceps Brachii primary confirmed. Brachialis is a key secondary in preacher curls but has no allowed mapping in the system (omitted per rules). Wrist Flexors secondary retained as forearm stabilizer during underhand kettlebell grip. Data valid.

Promoted chest (Sternal Head) from secondary to co-primary with Lats. EMG research (Journal of Applied Biomechanics, 2011) found pectoralis major is equally or more activated than latissimus dorsi in the pullover. Both muscles are prime movers in shoulder extension/adduction during this movement. Triceps and abs retained as secondary (Triceps stabilize the slight elbow bend; abs prevent rib flare). Anterior Deltoids would be a stabilizer but the exercise is a shoulder extension movement — chest co-primary is the correct biomechanical reading.

Added oblique (External Obliques + Internal Obliques) to secondary muscles. This is a unilateral hinge-row requiring anti-rotation core stability, consistent with the rule that unilateral exercises add oblique stabilization. Posterior Deltoid + Rhomboids/Upper Traps primary, and Lats (Latissimus Dorsi + Rotator Cuff) + Biceps secondary all confirmed by sources.
